Beltrami County District Court: A Comprehensive Guide

Contact Information and Hours

Location: Beltrami County Judicial Center
600 Minnesota Avenue NW, Suite 108
Bemidji, MN 56601

Hours of Operation:
Monday – Friday: 8:00 AM – 4:30 PM
Saturday & Sunday: Closed

Contact:
Phone: 218-333-4120
Fax: 218-333-4209
Website: www.mncourts.gov

Historical Background

The Beltrami County District Court has been serving the Bemidji community since 1866 when the county was established. As part of Minnesota's judicial system, it operates within one of the state's ten judicial districts under Minnesota Supreme Court oversight. In 1998, the court relocated to its current facility at 619 Beltrami Ave NW.

Court Structure and Operations

Jurisdiction

The court handles various legal matters within Beltrami County, including:

  • Civil cases (including those under $15,000)
  • Criminal cases (misdemeanors, gross misdemeanors, and felonies)
  • Family law matters
  • Probate cases
  • Real estate disputes

Court Personnel

The court operates with:

  • Four district court judges
  • Multiple court referees
  • Support staff including:
    • Court administrators
    • Court reporters
    • Law clerks
    • Probation officers
    • Clerical staff
    • Volunteer mediators
    • Guardians ad litem
    • Security personnel (sheriff deputies and court officers)

Legal Process Overview

Filing a Case

  1. Initial filing with court administrator
  2. Payment of applicable filing fees
  3. Service of process to involved parties
  4. Scheduling of first appearance or hearing

Court Proceedings

  • Initial appearances and arraignments
  • Pretrial conferences
  • Settlement negotiations
  • Trial proceedings (if necessary)
  • Sentencing hearings (for criminal cases)

Trial Process

  • Jury selection from county resident pool
  • Evidence presentation
  • Witness testimony
  • Jury deliberation
  • Verdict delivery
  • Post-trial proceedings

Online Resources and Services

Court Records Access

  • Minnesota Court Records Search System
  • Criminal history information database
  • Public case records
  • Court calendars and dockets

Digital Services

  • Online fine payment system
  • Electronic form submission
  • Court calendar access
  • Legal research tools

Available Forms and Documents

  • Civil case forms
  • Criminal case documents
  • Family law paperwork
  • Fee waiver applications
  • Self-help divorce forms
  • Expungement instructions

Legal Assistance and Support

Free Legal Resources

  • County law libraries
  • Self-help centers
  • Legal aid services
  • Public defender services
  • Problem-solving courts

Additional Support Services

  • Language interpretation
  • Disability accommodations
  • Child support services
  • Foreclosure assistance
  • Consumer protection resources

Important Guidelines

Court Etiquette

  • Professional dress required
  • No cell phones or electronic devices
  • Punctual attendance expected
  • Respectful behavior mandatory

Filing Fees

  • Civil cases: $100-300 base fee
  • Document copies: $1 per page
  • Fee waivers available for eligible individuals

Contact for Additional Information

For specific questions or concerns, contact the Court Administrator's office during business hours at 218-333-4120 or visit the courthouse in person.
